newsitem.title: FINLAND: Quinn sees EMU start on time, without Britain.
newsitem.headline: Quinn sees EMU start on time, without Britain.

text.p: Irish Finance Minister Ruairi Quinn said on Monday he expected the third stage of EMU to start on time in 1999, but that Britain would not be a member from the start despite its new more Europe-friendly government.

"...there is no reason to believe it will be postponed," Quinn told a news conference during a visit to Finland when asked whether he expected the third phase of European economic and monetary union to start on schedule.
"Giving the existing timetable it does not seem possible from a logistical point of view that Britain will be in a position to participate from January 1, 1999," Quinn said.
He referred to Britain's parliamentary process and to the referendum on EMU membership promised by Labour leader Tony Blair, the new prime minister.

"Britain will become more positive and constructive in its overall attitude to European issues," Quinn said. "We will get a first indication of that in the ECOFIN meeting next Monday," he added, referring to a regular meeting of European Union finance ministers in Brussels.
"We have seen the British labour government implement its commitment to participate in the social chapter," Quinn said. --Helsinki newsroom +358-9-680 50 245, news@reuters.fi
